{{Technical|date=September 2010}}
In [[financial mathematics]] (concerned with mathematical modeling of financial markets), the '''entropic risk measure''' is a [[risk measure]] which depends on the [[risk aversion]] of the user through the [[exponential utility]] function.  It is a possible alternative to other risk measures as [[value-at-risk]] or [[expected shortfall]].

It is a theoretically interesting measure because it provides different risk values for different individuals whose attitudes toward risk may differ. However, in practice it would be difficult to use since quantifying the risk aversion for an individual is difficult to do.  The entropic risk measure is the prime example of a [[convex risk measure]] which is not [[Coherent risk measure|coherent.]]<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Rudloff |first1=Birgit |last2=Sass |first2=Jorn |last3=Wunderlich |first3=Ralf |date=July 21, 2008 |contribution=Entropic Risk Constraints for Utility Maximization|title=Festschrift in celebration of Prof. Dr. Wilfried Greckschs 60th birthday|publisher=Shaker Verlag |contribution-url=http://www.princeton.edu/~brudloff/RudloffSassWunderlich08.pdf |accessdate=July 22, 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121018205712/http://www.princeton.edu/~brudloff/RudloffSassWunderlich08.pdf |archivedate=October 18, 2012 }}</ref>  Given the connection to [[utility function]]s, it can be used in [[utility maximization problem]]s.

==Mathematical definition==
The entropic risk measure with the risk aversion parameter <math>\theta > 0</math> is defined as
: <math>\rho^{\mathrm{ent}}(X) = \frac{1}{\theta}\log\left(\mathbb{E}[e^{-\theta X}]\right) = \sup_{Q \in \mathcal{M}_1} \left\{E^Q[-X] -\frac{1}{\theta}H(Q|P)\right\} \,</math><ref>{{cite book|first1=Hans|last1=Föllmer|first2=Alexander|last2=Schied|title=Stochastic finance: an introduction in discrete time|url=https://archive.org/details/stochasticcalcul02foll|url-access=limited|publisher=Walter de Gruyter|year=2004|edition=2|isbn=978-3-11-018346-7|page=[https://archive.org/details/stochasticcalcul02foll/page/n193 174]}}</ref>
where <math>H(Q|P) = E\left[\frac{dQ}{dP}\log\frac{dQ}{dP}\right]</math> is the [[relative entropy]] of ''Q'' [[Absolutely continuous#Absolute continuity of measures|<<]] ''P''.<ref name="FS10">{{Cite encyclopedia|last1=Follmer|first1=Hans|last2=Schied|first2=Alexander|date=October 8, 2008|title=Convex and Coherent Risk Measures|url=http://wws.mathematik.hu-berlin.de/~foellmer/papers/CCRM.pdf|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Quantitative Finance|accessdate=July 22, 2010|archive-date=July 19, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719042849/http://wws.mathematik.hu-berlin.de/~foellmer/papers/CCRM.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Acceptance set==
The [[acceptance set]] for the entropic risk measure is the set of payoffs with positive expected utility.  That is
: <math>A = \{X \in L^p(\mathcal{F}): E[u(X)] \geq 0\} = \{X \in L^p(\mathcal{F}): E\left[e^{-\theta X}\right] \leq 1\}</math>
where <math>u(X)</math> is the exponential utility function.<ref name="FS10" />

==Dynamic entropic risk measure==
The [[conditional risk measure]] associated with dynamic entropic risk with risk aversion parameter <math>\theta</math> is given by
:<math>\rho^{\mathrm{ent}}_t(X) = \frac{1}{\theta}\log\left(\mathbb{E}[e^{-\theta X} | \mathcal{F}_t]\right).</math>
This is a [[time consistent]] risk measure if <math>\theta</math> is constant through time,
<ref name="penner_thesis">{{cite thesis|last=Penner |first=Irina |year=2007 |title=Dynamic convex risk measures: time consistency, prudence, and sustainability |publisher=Humboldt University of Berlin|doi=10.18452/15745 }}</ref> and can be computed efficiently using [[Stochastic differential equation|forward-backwards differential equations]]<ref name="Wang_thesis">{{cite journal
|last1=Hyndman |first1=Cody |last2=Kratsios |first2=Anastasis |last3=Wang |first3=Renjie |year=2020 |title= The entropic measure transform|journal=Canadian Journal of Statistics |volume=48 |pages=97–129 |doi=10.1002/cjs.11537 |arxiv=1511.06032 |s2cid=159089174 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1002/cjs.11537 |format=pdf}}</ref>
<ref name="Thelia">{{cite journal|last1=Chong |first1=Wing Fung |last2=Hu |first2=Ying |last3=Liang |first3=Gechun |last4= Zariphopoulou |first4=Thaleia |year=2019 |title= An ergodic BSDE approach to forward entropic risk measures: representation and large-maturity behavior|journal=Finance and Stochastics |volume=23 |pages=239–273 |doi=10.1007/s00780-018-0377-3 |s2cid=16261697 |doi-access=free |arxiv=1607.02289 }}</ref>
.
